channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Zelensky Responds to US Leader's Call for New Leadership, Links Elections to Putin's Truce
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that Ukraine would hold elections if Russian President Putin agreed to a 60-day truce. This response comes after the US leader suggested it was time for Ukraine to choose new leadership. The specifics of the truce and election conditions remain to be detailed.

item.title: National Bank of Kazakhstan Reports Stable Dollar Exchange Rate on October 12
item.description: The National Bank of Kazakhstan announced the exchange rates for the dollar, euro, and ruble in Astana and Almaty for October 12. In Astana, the dollar was bought at 448.99 tenge and sold at 455.99 tenge. The euro was bought at 501.96 and sold at 511.96 tenge, while the ruble was traded at 5.17 tenge for buying and 5.37 for selling.

item.title: Kazakhstan Adjusts Exports to Iran: Reduced Barley, Increased Oilseeds and Wheat
item.description: Kazakhstan's trade with Iran reached $272.9 million in January-August, unchanged year-on-year. While barley exports to Iran decreased significantly, shipments of vegetable oils and wheat saw substantial growth. Kazakhstan also began exporting rapeseed, soybeans, and vinyl chloride polymers to Iran for the first time this year.

item.title: Kazakhstan Closes Four Criminal Cases Against Illegal Microfinance Organizations Under Amnesty
item.description: Kazakhstan has closed four criminal cases against illegal microfinance organizations (MFOs) under an amnesty program since the beginning of the year. Out of 19 investigated cases, 10 have been sent to court. The General Prosecutor's Office is investigating platforms like Alem Credit for illegal activities, including high interest rates and data collection.

item.title: Canada Plans to Increase Oil and Diesel Exports to the United States
item.description: Canada intends to increase its diesel fuel supply to the United States, according to Prime Minister Mark Carney. This decision follows a phone call with U.S. President Donald Trump. Canada aims to maximize oil and diesel exports, with current daily diesel deliveries exceeding one million barrels. Russia also confirmed its readiness to supply oil products to the U.S. and global markets.

item.title: Surveillance Cameras Emerge as Effective Intelligence Tools in the Middle East, WSJ Reports
item.description: Internet-connected surveillance cameras worldwide are becoming valuable sources of military intelligence, according to the Wall Street Journal. Hackers can exploit these devices to monitor strategic locations and enemy troop movements, potentially proving more effective than traditional spies in the Middle East. Approximately 1.2 billion such cameras are currently in use globally.

item.title: Kazakhstan and University of Arizona to Expand Cooperation in Water Sector
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation and the University of Arizona are developing a roadmap for cooperation. This includes joint seminars, training courses, and internships for Kazakh specialists, developing hydrological models tailored to the country's specifics, and implementing joint projects on sustainable water resource management under climate change.

item.title: Yandex Outage: Risks to Personal Data of Kazakhstan Citizens Addressed
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development stated that concerns about Kazakh citizens' personal data due to Yandex service disruptions are unfounded. Servers storing personal data are located within Kazakhstan and operating normally. However, some components for taxi and delivery services are located outside the country, requiring a comprehensive solution for data storage and platform stability.

item.title: Tanker Attacks Near Oman Coast: UK Maritime Trade Warns of Danger
item.description: A drone attacked a tanker near Oman's Sohar port on October 11, with two Indian sailors missing. The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported another tanker hit exiting the Strait of Hormuz, sustaining damage but no crew injuries. These incidents heighten concerns for shipping security in the vital Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: New Flooding in Nepal After Landslide Blocks River
item.description: Authorities in Nepal urged villagers to evacuate after a landslide in Gorkha district blocked the Budhi Gandaki river, causing downstream flooding. Several houses and infrastructure, including bridges and a hydropower camp, were damaged. 49 people were rescued, but five remain missing. This follows a catastrophic August flood.

item.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport result in casualties
item.description: Houthi forces launched two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia over the weekend. The first strike reportedly killed at least 13 people and injured over 300. A second attack resulted in one fatality and 11 injuries, according to the country's Civil Aviation Authority. The Houthis claimed responsibility and warned airlines against using Saudi airports.

item.title: Pakistan declares emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan, dismisses provincial government
item.description: Pakistan's President Arif Alvi approved the imposition of emergency rule in the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, bordering Afghanistan. The regional government of Imran Khan's PTI party has been removed from administration. Federal authorities cited a deteriorating security situation and an increase in armed group attacks as reasons for the decision, which could last up to six months.

item.title: Kazakhstan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expresses solidarity with Riyadh
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian civilian infrastructure, which resulted in casualties. The ministry stated that such attacks violate international law and are unacceptable. Kazakhstan called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and urged the resolution of the crisis through political and diplomatic means, expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Anti-Drone Measures Implemented at Turkmenbashi Airport During Putin's Arrival
item.description: Anti-drone measures were reportedly taken at Turkmenbashi airport and the nearby Avaza resort area between October 7-9 during international events attended by CIS and Iranian leaders. Sources observed moving lights, possibly interceptor drones, and searchlights in the sky before President Putin's arrival. No incidents were reported.

item.title: Lukashenko Silent on Turkmenistan's Debt for Garlyk Mining Plant Construction
item.description: During a meeting with Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow in Avaza, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko reportedly did not raise the issue of Turkmenistan's debt to Belgorhimprom for the construction of the Garlyk mining and processing plant. Turkmenistan's expenses for international arbitration in this case have risen to at least $26.5 million.

item.title: Kazakhstan: New Sports University Linked to President's Family Faces Scrutiny
item.description: A new sports university in Astana, established by presidential decree, is facing public debate due to its founder's familial ties to President Tokayev. The 23-year-old founder, Nurassyl Medeu, is the grandson of the president's sister. While the state funded the campus, a private entity holds 95% ownership.

item.title: Afghanistan Shifts Pharmaceutical Sourcing from Pakistan to India and Russia
item.description: Afghanistan's pharmaceutical market is diversifying, reducing dependence on Pakistan. Political disputes and trade route closures have prompted this shift. India is emerging as a major supplier of medicines and medical equipment, with Russia also entering the market. This move signals a potential transformation in Afghanistan's supply chain, aiming for reduced reliance on single sources.

item.title: NetBlocks Reports Widespread Internet Disruption in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province
item.description: NetBlocks reports widespread internet disruptions in parts of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. This occurs amid the declaration of a state of emergency and the arrest of the provincial chief minister. The emergency was declared following protests by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party demanding the release of former Prime Minister Imran Khan.

item.title: Nepal Flooding: Infrastructure Damaged, Hydropower Plant Affected, Several Missing
item.description: A new flood in central Nepal, near the capital Kathmandu, has caused significant damage. The flood, triggered by a natural dam breach, destroyed bridges, damaged a local hydropower plant, and left five people missing. The area is still recovering from a previous catastrophic flood in late August 2026.

item.title: At Least 72 Workers Killed in Airstrike on Gold Mine Near Egypt-Sudan Border
item.description: A Sudanese human rights group reports that at least 72 workers were killed in an airstrike on a gold mine near the Egypt-Sudan border. The Emergency Lawyers organization accused the Egyptian army of carrying out the attack on Saturday. This is the second such attack in the area this year.

item.title: UN Project Equips Over 833 Afghan Schools and Health Centers with Solar Power
item.description: The UN Development Programme in Afghanistan has equipped 833 schools and health centers with solar power, benefiting over 812,000 women and girls. The project also trained 20 women in solar energy systems, aiming to expand access to renewable energy and improve opportunities for women and girls.

item.title: Young Man Killed by Unidentified Gunmen in Afghanistan's Nangarhar Province
item.description: A young man named Ismail was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in the Surkh Rod district of Nangarhar province. The motive behind the killing remains unclear. This incident follows a recent increase in criminal activities, targeted killings, and armed robberies across several Afghan provinces.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Explains Why Yandex Outages Affected Services in the Country
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development clarified that servers storing user data for Yandex services are operating normally, despite company-wide outages. While personal data servers are located within Kazakhstan, some components for taxi and delivery services are hosted abroad. The ministry is working with Yandex on recovery and enhancing service resilience.

item.title: King Philippe of Belgium Expresses Desire to Get to Know Kazakhstan Better During State Visit
item.description: King Philippe of Belgium, upon arrival in Astana, met with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The King thanked the President for the warm welcome and expressed his hope for successful negotiations, stating a desire to become better acquainted with Kazakhstan during the three-day state visit. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral relations and multifaceted partnership.

item.title: Residents of Munaily District to Receive Free Legal Consultations in Mangystau Region
item.description: On October 12, residents of Munaily District in the Mangystau Region can receive free legal consultations during a mobile legal caravan event. The meeting, held at the new Public Service Center parking lot, aims to increase legal literacy and prevent offenses by connecting citizens with legal experts and authorities.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev and Belgian King Philippe Exchange Greetings in Astana Airport
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium upon their arrival in Astana for a state visit. Tokayev highlighted the historical significance of the visit for strengthening bilateral ties and noted Kazakhstan's economic growth. King Philippe thanked the President for the warm reception and expressed optimism for productive negotiations and deeper partnership.

item.title: Kazakh President Holds Brief Conversation with Belgian Royal Guests at Airport Hall
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held a brief conversation with the King and Queen of Belgium in the airport hall, emphasizing the historical significance of their visit for strengthening Kazakh-Belgian relations. The President noted the country's development and economic growth, predicting the visit would boost bilateral ties. The King thanked the President for the hospitality and expressed confidence in successful negotiations.

item.title: Taliban Intelligence Arrests Son of Former Jihadist Commander in Badghis
item.description: Taliban intelligence forces have reportedly arrested Haroon, the son of prominent former jihadist commander Abdulkhaliq Khan Chakar, in Badghis Province. Haroon, who held no government position under the previous administration and was involved in private business, was arrested on Friday. The reasons for his detention by the Taliban remain unclear.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis Claim Attacks on Riyadh Airport and Saudi Energy Facilities
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels announced multiple attacks targeting Riyadh's airport and Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree stated that ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones were used in four operations over 24 hours. Targets included Riyadh's airport multiple times, Dammam airport, and two facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco. Saudi authorities confirmed an attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport injured several people.

item.title: US Congress Drafts Bill to Ban Russian Oil Imports
item.description: A bill is being prepared in the US Congress to ban the purchase of Russian oil. Proposed by House member Brian Fitzpatrick, the legislation aims to prohibit all types of Russian oil purchases, following Ronald Reagan's 'peace through strength' policy.

item.title: Belgian Royal Couple's Flight Escorted by Kazakh Air Force Jets
item.description: The aircraft carrying the Belgian King Philippe and Queen Mathilde was escorted by Kazakh Air Force fighter jets from the border to Astana. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed the royal couple upon their arrival for a state visit. An honor guard and presidential orchestra were present.

item.title: Head of State Welcomes King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium at Astana airport as they arrived for a state visit. Kazakh Air Force jets escorted their plane from the border to the capital. A formal reception with an honor guard and presidential orchestra took place.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Discusses Cooperation with OIC Deputy Secretary-General
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's foreign minister, met with OIC Assistant Secretary-General Tarig Ali Bakheet to discuss expanding cooperation. The meeting covered the OIC's new secretary-general, the Taliban's role, and regional and global political and economic developments. Both sides emphasized strengthening relations and creating new cooperation opportunities.

item.title: UNICEF: Over 28% of Afghan Women Aged 20-24 Married Before 18
item.description: UNICEF reports that 28.7% of Afghan women aged 20-24 were married before 18, with rates reaching one in two girls in some regions. Child marriage threatens girls' health, education, and future opportunities, increasing risks of violence and early pregnancy complications. UNICEF urges the Taliban to reopen girls' secondary schools.

item.title: Two Uzbek Citizens Lightly Injured in Ballistic Missile Attack on Riyadh Airport
item.description: Two Uzbek citizens sustained minor injuries during a ballistic missile attack on Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on October 10. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Uzbekistan confirmed the incident, stating that the injured received medical attention and were later discharged. The Uzbek embassy is monitoring the situation and providing consular assistance.

item.title: UNICEF Urges Action to End Child Marriage and Promote Girls' Education in Afghanistan
item.description: On International Day of the Girl, UNICEF Afghanistan called for urgent measures to end child marriage. The organization emphasized girls' right to education, development, and a safe life, stating that child marriage hinders their future. UNICEF suggested investing in girls' education, reforming laws, and strengthening social support systems as preventive strategies.

item.title: Two Uzbek Citizens Injured in Rocket Attack on Saudi Airport, Foreign Ministry Reports
item.description: Two Uzbek citizens were injured in a rocket attack on an airport in Saudi Arabia, according to the Uzbek Foreign Ministry. Approximately 20 other Uzbek citizens were present at the airport during the incident and were reportedly unharmed. Further details are being investigated.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Demand for Bank Loans Increases, Driven by Consumer Needs
item.description: The demand for bank loans among individuals in Uzbekistan has significantly increased. The total amount of loans issued to individuals grew by 23.3 trillion UZS over eight months. This indicates a rising trend in borrowing for various personal purposes across the country.

item.title: Pakistan Faces Interconnected Political, Security, and Economic Crises
item.description: Pakistan is currently grappling with significant political, security, and economic challenges. These interconnected crises are impacting the nation's stability and development. Further details on the specific nature and extent of these issues were not provided in the source material.

item.title: IOM Reports 54% of Returnees to Afghanistan Cannot Meet Basic Needs
item.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has reported that 54 percent of individuals returning to Afghanistan are unable to meet their basic needs. This highlights significant challenges faced by returnees in the country, impacting their ability to sustain themselves.
